cycles.method: Not counted in chip cycles: the owner waived chip worst-case cycles for 0.2.2 (sdk/approvals/repitch-build-approval.json, chip-worst-case-cycles), as for 0.2.1. Repitch's frame-interrupt work is its ev_play_increment handler (repitch_play_increment), which sets a REPITCH track's playback increment when the increment builder recomputes; while repitch_in_use answers 0 the base puts stock's bytes back under rate_gate and pitch_gate and the handler leaves the frame. repitch_in_use runs on the UI tick, outside the frame interrupt. In the ColdFire interpreter, on the 0.2.2 build before the 25 November 2026 sweep trim (package c97b00a4), 288 playback-increment cases took at most 28 instructions in the handler, and 3,072 stored Part and track cases with 5,760 sample lookups took at most 489 instructions for the all-active sweep of repitch_in_use. The trimmed sweep (half a Part a tick, at most 6 bank reads) was not counted; five emulator calls of it pass (TESTING.md).

load.method: No cfmeter.py capture under a flood; the owner waived current-build hardware evidence for 0.2.2. Measured instead with npm run device:price on the owner's MKII (OS 1.40C), development twin be86323a of base 0.7.11, 20 November 2026, package c97b00a4 (0.2.2 before the 25 November sweep trim), A01 on Part 4 with seven triggered FLEX tracks, two 8 s windows: the frame interrupt read 51.4 % and 51.4 % with no module, 51.6 % and 51.5 % with Repitch installed and used nowhere (+0.2 and +0.1 points), against +2.2 for the published 0.2.1 on the same base and scene, with zero skipped renders in all five windows. In use, on a development twin (9203cdf6) of base 0.7.14, 22 November 2026, a scene where T5's loop resolves REPITCH: 0.2.1 and 0.2.2 both added +2.7 points (42.1 % against 39.4 %). The trimmed build was not measured on the unit; on 25 November the untrimmed sweep added about 20 us to every UI tick (development twin 493c9cc5 of base 0.8.1, stopped, profile:3), which the trim addresses.
